chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAmr ibn Ibrāhīm, from Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from Hārūn ibn Ḥukaym al-Arqaṭ, the maternal uncle of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I came to him for a need and found him in the bathhouse applying depilatory. So I mentioned my need to him, and he said: “Will you not apply depilatory?” I said: “I only used it most recently the day before yesterday.” He said: “Apply it, for indeed al-nūrah is a purifier.”

key_terms.النُّورَةَ: lime-based depilatory used for hair removal
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse, the setting in which the encounter took place
key_terms.حَاجَتِي: my need or request brought before him
key_terms.طَهُورٌ: a purifier; something possessing purifying quality
key_terms.يَطَّلِي: applying depilatory treatment to the body

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about using al-nūrah in the bathhouse?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an encounter in the bathhouse in which the Imam عليه السلام encourages the use of depilatory. It indicates the purifying quality of al-nūrah and reflects etiquette and practical guidance connected to taharah and personal grooming.
